head: a0aa5ab2
note: Pseudo-code written by the reviewing agent; explain_check.py verifies every step against the cited lines.

steps.text: a shared sample `TestSource` with an int-keyed `MyObject`, a string-keyed `MyStringKeyObject`, an enum `MyEnum`, a union `IMyUnion` with member `MyUnionMember`, and a resolver `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`
`RunGeneratorAsync` runs the source generator once on that sample and returns each generated file's path and text
the helper throws away the generator's diagnostics and the updated compilation (`out _, out _`)
it asserts at least five files came out (`generated.Count >= 5`)
it asserts every generated file's text contains the attribute (`text.Contains(ExcludeAttribute)`)

does_not_check: It checks the attribute appears at least once per file, not that every type in the file carries it.
It does not compile the generated code, and generator errors would go unnoticed.
notes: Fails on base (the resolver file has no attribute) and passes on the branch.

steps.text: `Guard` is the line `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`, meant to hide the attribute from targets said not to have it
`RunGeneratorAsync(TestSource)` runs the generator on the shared sample
for each generated file, Windows line endings are turned into plain newlines (`text.Replace("\r\n", "\n")`)
it counts all occurrences of the attribute, and separately the occurrences that sit in the exact block: guard line, attribute line (indented by one tab or not at all), `#endif`
it asserts the file has at least one attribute (`attributeCount > 0`) and that every one is guarded (`Assert.Equal(attributeCount, guardedCount)`)

does_not_check: It does not compile the generated code for netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework, so it does not show those consumers still build.
It does not check that the guard is needed; our evidence says the attribute exists on both targets (C-2297-08).
notes: Fails on base (no attribute in the resolver file) and passes on the branch.
